terms.meaning: A named style option, such as urgent or gray, that picks a set of colors.
A label added to an element that tells the styling system how to draw it.
A small function that combines several class names into one string, dropping empty ones.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the badge
sections.what: Brings in React and the class-combining helper.
sections.why: Likely reason: the helper merges this badge's base style with the colors and any extra styles the caller adds.
sections.watch_out: Any class name the caller passes can override the built-in look, so colors may change in ways the badge does not control.

sections.name: BadgeProps
sections.title: Allowed badge variants and their props
sections.what: Lists the allowed looks: urgent, high, medium, low, emerald, cyan, amber, indigo and gray. Also accepts the label text and optional extra styles.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed list keeps colors the same across screens.
sections.watch_out: A look name outside this list gives a badge with no color set and no error.

sections.name: Badge
sections.title: Badge drawing and color table
sections.what: Draws a small rounded label with bold uppercase text, using the colors chosen by its variant. Defaults to indigo if no variant is given.
sections.why: Likely reason: the uppercase bold style keeps short labels easy to read.
sections.watch_out: Urgent and high share the same red, and medium and amber share the same orange, so those pairs cannot be told apart by color.

summary: A small colored label used to show priority or status, such as URGENT or DOING.
purpose: Give tags a consistent look and a color that matches their meaning.
why: Likely reason: colored tags let users spot priority and status at a glance.
how: 1. Takes a variant name, the label text, and any extra styles. 2. Looks up the colors for that variant, defaulting to indigo if none is given. 3. Combines the base style, the colors and the extra styles. 4. Draws a small span with the label inside.
inputs: A variant name such as urgent, high, medium, low, emerald, cyan, amber, indigo or gray; the label text; optional extra class names.
outputs: A styled label on screen. Nothing is saved.
risks: A variant name outside the list gives a badge with no color and no error. Urgent and high share one color, and medium and amber share another.
debug: If a badge has the wrong color, check the variant string the caller passes, then the color table in this file. If a badge is plain, the variant name is probably misspelled.
